column1: Ukraine has agreed to supply up to 1.2 million rounds to the European Union this year. That amount includes a total of €1bn in the first phase, of which €1.1bn is to be shared from the EU, followed by a further €1bn on the Ukrainian side.
Ukraine's defence ministry said last month that it had delivered 10,000 rounds to the European Union on its own.
The amount of the first round is expected to be divided among the EU bloc's 28 member states.
The EU also agreed last month to provide up to €2.5bn this year to Ukraine for the first phase of the joint operations programme. The money will be paid in the new year.
The EU has agreed to pay the amount for its "equipment and supplies" so that Ukraine can begin its combat training next year.
The EU's defence minister said last week Ukraine had agreed with France and Britain that they would pay $150m for the first round of its joint training programme.
EU: 'If we can't do it we will'
The EU's defence minister said last week that "if we cannot do it we will"
Ukrainian Prime Minister Arseniy Yatsenyuk said he could not accept Britain's decision to deliver its own rounds to the EU.
Yatsenyuk, who is due to meet with EU leaders in Brussels this week, said he would agree to the deal even if it was "unacceptable".
British Prime Minister Theresa May said she would not "accept this deal".
The agreement had been negotiated by the EU's military chiefs last month but has been delayed in the face of the growing number of Russian military exercises in Ukraine.
Ukraine's defence ministry said in a statement that it "could not be a good idea" for the military alliance to send its own rounds to the EU after the first round.
The Ukrainian military also said that it could not help with the deliveries of its own round.
